title: Classification and phylogeny; Evidence for evolution
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EV06c#t1 term and clue written for the game; EV06c#t3 term and clue written for the game; EV06b#t1 term and clue written for the game; EV06c#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EV03a#N.3a, EV06b#N.3, EV06c#N.7, EV03a#N.5a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Domain
items.clue: Level of classification above kingdom; life has three

items.label: Eukarya
items.clue: Top-level group containing Protoctista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia

items.label: Common ancestor
items.clue: Shared more recently by relatives whose base sequences show fewer differences

items.label: Ribosomal RNA
items.clue: Molecule whose base sequences Woese and Fox compared across many organisms in 1977

questions.stem: Sharks, which are fish, and dolphins, which are mammals, both have streamlined bodies, a dorsal fin and paddle-shaped front fins. Which statement about these features is correct?

options.text: They are homologous, showing that dolphins are more closely related to sharks than they are to other mammals.
They are homologous, because in both animals the features perform the same function in water.
They show that the two species are converging on each other and will eventually merge into a single species.
They are analogous: they evolved separately because similar selection favoured similar shapes in water.

questions.stem: Using the cytochrome c data, which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Humans evolved from chimpanzees, because their cytochrome c sequences are identical.
Humans share a more recent common ancestor with the dog than with the tuna.
The tuna is the least evolved of these animals, because its protein differs most from ours.
The dog and the chicken differ from each other at 2 positions, since 13 − 11 = 2.

questions.explanation: 11 differences against 21. Differences accumulate after lineages split, so fewer differences mean a more recent common ancestor.

questions.stem: Which evidence was used in 1977 to propose that all organisms should be classified into three domains?

options.text: Visible differences in cell structure seen using the electron microscope.
Evidence that archaea are a subgroup of bacteria, so that all prokaryotes form one domain.
Overall similarity in the appearance and way of life of the organisms being classified.
Comparison of the base sequences of ribosomal RNA across many different organisms.

questions.explanation: rRNA base sequences showed that prokaryotes form two groups, each as different from the other as from eukaryotes.

questions.stem: The amino acid sequence of the same protein was compared in four species. Compared with species W, species X differs at 2 positions, species Y at 15 positions and species Z at 31 positions. Which conclusion is supported by the data?

options.text: W shares a more recent common ancestor with X than it does with either Y or Z.
Z is the most primitive of the four species, because its sequence is furthest from W's.
X lives in the same kind of habitat as W, because similar conditions give similar proteins.
X is the ancestor of W, because the two sequences are almost identical.

questions.explanation: Differences accumulate after two lineages split. W and X differ least, so their common ancestor is the most recent.
